subject: Budget range validation: monthly spend band + procurement thresholds
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Li <alex@paybridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Budget range validation: monthly spend band + procurement thresholds

Alex — thanks for taking the call today. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on so we can align on pricing and procurement next steps.

Summary of discovery:
- Primary workload: customer support summarization + routing + a small search re-ranker.
- Expected token profile: short prompts (~30–60 tokens) + 60–200 token responses.
- Volume cadence: pilot (Q4): ~10M tokens/month; expected ramp to 50–120M tokens/month post-launch (Q1). Upside scenarios to 200M+/month in year 1.

Cost / unit economics items we discussed:
- You called out a target unit economics band of ~$700–$900 per 1M tokens (post-discount) as the number that keeps the feature P&L green.
- Based on that, rough monthly spend bands are: 10M -> $7k–$9k; 50M -> $35k–$45k; 120M -> $84k–$108k; 200M -> $140k–$180k.

Procurement thresholds / requirements you flagged:
- A PO is required for any commitment over ~$30k/month (they escalate to procurement/legal).
- Typical procurement lead time: 4–6 weeks for standard PO + SLA; longer if additional security addenda are needed.

Immediate asks from our side:
1) Can you confirm the expected month-by-month ramp (pilot -> month 1/3/6 post-launch)? rough numbers are fine.
2) Confirm whether embeddings traffic is included in the same bucket or priced separately (you mentioned embeddings will be used for search).
3) Any procurement constraints on contract length or auto-renew clauses?

Attachments: I’m attaching a simple pricing worksheet (redwood_pricing_1M_tokens.xlsx) with illustrative tiers — will update once we confirm volumes.

Next steps: I’ll draft a short one-pager with committed-tier pricing + sample PO language for procurement to review. Can we aim to get that into your procurement team by Nov 16 to hit a Dec/Jan procurement window?

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(d) 415-555-0123 | dylan@redwood.com
From: Alex Li <alex@paybridge.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Budget range validation: monthly spend band + procurement thresholds

Thanks, Dylan — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Volume ramp: pilot (Dec): 8–12M/mo; month 1 post-launch (Jan): 30–40M/mo; month 3: ~80–120M/mo. Long term (12mo) target ~150–200M/mo assuming product hits retention targets.
- Embeddings: search will be a smaller percentage initially (~10–15% of token volume) but we prefer embeddings priced separately if possible (different model).
- Procurement: internal rule — any vendor spend that exceeds $25k/quarter or $75k/year needs PO + SOW. For monthly recurring commitments >$30k we need procurement review.

Can you share the per-1M-token price bands for both generation and embeddings (we care about blended and model-specific pricing)? Also include any committed-discount examples for a 12-month commit.

Natalie (cc) is our procurement lead and will be pulled in once we have a ballpark number she can vet.

Appreciate the quick turnaround —
Alex Li
Head of ML Ops | Paybridge
alex@paybridge.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Budget range validation — pricing posture suggestion

Dylan — forwarding my notes / suggested pricing posture before you send the one-pager to Alex/Natalie. Quick thoughts:

- Given their ramp profile (pilot -> 120M), we should lead with a tiered committed pricing approach and provide an uncommitted (pay-as-you-go) option for the pilot. That reduces procurement friction while giving them the economics they want as they scale.

Proposed illustrative tiers (generation model):
- 0–10M tokens/month (pilot): $1,200 / 1M tokens (pay-as-you-go or short-term trial rate)
- 10–50M tokens/month: $900 / 1M tokens (committed tier discount)
- 50–200M tokens/month: $750 / 1M tokens (higher commit discount)
- >200M/month: custom enterprise pricing (include additional SLA/throughput guarantees)

Embeddings: list separately — recommended $600 / 1M tokens for 0–50M, $450 / 1M for 50–200M (embeddings model, different cost basis).

Procurement thresholds to call out in the one-pager:
- PO required for commitments > $30k/month or multi-month prepayment > $75k.
- Standard 30-day net payment; 90-day exceptions need commercial review.

Ask: Dylan, put these numbers into the one-pager and include 3 scenarios (pilot, steady-state, aggressive) with monthly and annualized spend and the link to the HubSpot deal. Also call out a recommended initial commitment (6–12 months) to unlock the 50–200M pricing band.

If they push back on the pilot rate, we can offer a small pilot credit ($5k) or a usage credit applied toward the first invoice of a committed term.

-Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Li <alex@paybridge.com>, Natalie Gomez <natalie@paybridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Budget range validation: monthly spend band + procurement thresholds — one-pager attached

Alex / Natalie — attaching a short one-pager that lays out the tiers Marissa suggested and three illustrative scenarios (pilot, steady-state, aggressive ramp). Attachment: paybridge_pricing_onepager.pdf.

Highlights:
- Pilot option: pay-as-you-go at $1,200 / 1M (or 2-week free pilot credit up to 10M).
- Committed tiers (example): 10–50M @ $900 / 1M; 50–200M @ $750 / 1M. Embeddings priced separately as noted.
- Based on your ramp, a 6–12 month commitment to a 50M/month floor gets you into the $750 band and keeps monthly spend in the ~$40k–$150k range.
- Procurement notes: PO required for >$30k/month; typical procurement lead time 4–6 weeks. We can provide standard PO language and a short SOW for Natalie to review.

Next steps:
1) Can Natalie confirm the internal procurement trigger and timeline?
2) Alex, can you confirm the month-by-month ramp (pilot -> M1 -> M3 -> M6) so I can model ARR and provide a short MPP (mutual performance plan)?
3) If acceptable, I’ll put a draft commitment schedule into the HubSpot deal and propose a 30-minute review next Tue (Nov 16) to align procurement + engineering requirements (SSO, SOC2 evidence). HubSpot link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/8910

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
